approaches.name: Compose established libraries per layer, hand-roll only the domain core
approaches.summary: Use mature PyPI and npm packages for every commodity layer (SQLAlchemy 2 async on python-oracledb, Alembic, FastAPI, pydantic v2 and pydantic-settings, sse-starlette for SSE, the OCI SDK, the anthropic SDK, cohere[oci] for Reader B, and shadcn/ui plus Zod, openapi-typescript and eslint/vitest on the web side). Hand-roll only what CLAUDE.md marks as domain logic: the generic repository, the unit of work, StageRunner, the status enum, the matcher scorer and the auto-fix handlers.
how: api/: uv project; SQLAlchemy 2.0 async engine via oracle+oracledb (SQLAlchemy supports one dialect name for sync and async), python-oracledb in thin mode with the ATP wallet.
Alembic for migrations; pydantic-settings for stories #27 and #28 config loading; FastAPI plus sse-starlette for SSE.
LLM layer: anthropic SDK for Opus and Haiku with structured outputs; cohere[oci] OciClientV2 (or OCI SDK directly) for Reader B with servingType DEDICATED.
web/: openapi-typescript generated types from FastAPI OpenAPI, Zod at boundaries, shadcn primitives from the CLI, eslint and vitest.
Hand-rolled: BaseRepository, UnitOfWork, StageRunner, one status module, money helpers, matcher, auto-fix engine.
evidence: SQLAlchemy docs: the oracledb dialect serves sync and async; create_async_engine with oracle+oracledb:// selects async (sqlalchemy.org dialects/oracle docs, 2.1 page).
python-oracledb docs (Appendix D): SQLAlchemy 2 supports python-oracledb directly; thin mode is the default and needs no Oracle client libraries.
Cohere Python SDK on PyPI (cohere 7.x) ships OciClient and OciClientV2 under the cohere[oci] extra; Oracle's April 2026 post describes the swap as a small change.
docs/reference/prior-implementation-lessons.md sections 3 and 7 already list the Fusion and bus facts to port, so no library has to be chosen for those rules.
Not verified: exact PyPI version numbers, and whether cohere[oci] supports servingType DEDICATED for Command A Vision; the search results were inconclusive on dedicated serving and vision.
risks: The cohere[oci] client may not support DEDICATED endpoints or Command A Vision; fall back to the raw OCI SDK behind the same LlmClient interface.
SQLAlchemy async with oracledb is a moderately sparse path; expect dialect quirks around JSON and VECTOR types.
Dependency sprawl across api and web must be pinned; the two-week-old version rule applies to CDN scripts only, not PyPI, so pin deliberately.

approaches.name: Adopt a PyPI transactional-outbox library for the bus
approaches.summary: Replace the hand-rolled outbox table, relay and lease logic with an existing PyPI outbox package and keep the rest of the runtime custom.
how: Candidates from search: pactix (outbox and inbox on async SQLAlchemy, leases, FIFO, Kafka transport extra), pgrelay (SKIP LOCKED worker, leases), faststream-outbox (requires Python 3.13+ and PostgreSQL 12+).
Enqueue inside the same SQLAlchemy session as the work item, so state and event commit together.
Relay publishes to OCI Streaming through its Kafka-compatible endpoint with an aiokafka or confluent producer.
Keep StageRunner and the status enum custom.
evidence: pactix, pgrelay and faststream-outbox are PostgreSQL-oriented (search results, PyPI pages). ATP is Oracle, so the SKIP LOCKED and table DDL assumptions do not carry over.
python-outbox-core is built around Kafka and FastStream; qx-db is tied to the Qx framework.
smixi/python-outbox is described as unmaintained; the others have unverified release activity.
risks: Postgres-only SQL and DDL would need rewriting for Oracle, which defeats the reuse.
Lease and retry semantics would have to match the auto-fix and lock rules in CLAUDE.md (story #40), so the library's model may not fit.
Adds a dependency that owns part of the system of record, against the rule that the database is the system of record.

approaches.name: Hand-roll the outbox on Oracle, with a generic SOAP library for Fusion
approaches.summary: Write a small outbox and relay on ATP (identity PK, SKIP LOCKED claim) and use a generic SOAP client library for the Fusion apply, BIP and attachment calls, with only the fault parsing custom.
how: Outbox table as a SQLAlchemy model in the data layer; relay claims rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and publishes via aiokafka with SASL_SSL.
Fusion: zeep (PyPI) for WSDL-driven SOAP calls to StandardReceiptService and BIP ExternalReportWSSService; hand-written fail-closed parsing of faults inside HTTP 200 envelopes.
Fusion REST through httpx with retry and backoff (tenacity), and a typed error mapping layer.
Keep StageRunner and the status enum custom.
evidence: CLAUDE.md requires the outbox in the same transaction and SKIP LOCKED on ATP, which this option meets without a foreign library.
prior-implementation-lessons.md section 3 says faults arrive inside HTTP 200 envelopes and that some codes must be ignored. zeep would not handle that for us, so this part stays custom either way.
Not verified: zeep and aiokafka versions and their async support; no search was run for them.
risks: Hand-rolled relay and retry code is the most likely source of the lost-event defects the lessons doc describes.
zeep is synchronous, so Fusion calls would need to run in a thread pool to stay async end to end.
More custom code means more tests, and the tests run only in BMN's test cycles.
